rounds.text: Vasa Denticity Ltd currently trades at a significant valuation premium, with a P/E ratio of 70.35x compared to the sector benchmark of 32.16x [E6]. This aggressive pricing is further reflected in an EV/EBITDA of 47.07x, which is nearly triple the sector benchmark of 17.13x [E11]. The company’s fundamental performance fails to justify these multiples, as evidenced by a compounded profit growth of -29% over the trailing twelve months [E15] and a concerning operating cash flow of Rs -25 Cr [E25]. Furthermore, the business is currently destroying value through its cash conversion cycle, which stands at -2.50x due to negative operating cash flow relative to reported profit [E24]. The stock’s internal health is also challenged by a declining promoter stake, which has fallen by 9.43 percentage points over the last three years [E32, E56]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong current ratio of 8.01x [E29] and is effectively debt-free [E28, E50]. Despite these liquidity strengths, the disconnect between the current market price and the intrinsic value calculated by a discounted cash flow model suggests a margin of safety of -216.8% [E36, E37].
